<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f2ad6edb963501f8e425965926e93a456c706363` — the merge of head `21b30f4b7982d22878115907dbb805b6ede7aa39` into base `e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f2ad6edb963501f8e425965926e93a456c706363 && git checkout f2ad6edb963501f8e425965926e93a456c706363
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05 21b30f4b7982d22878115907dbb805b6ede7aa39 && git checkout -B drift-repro e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05 && git merge --no-ff 21b30f4b7982d22878115907dbb805b6ede7aa39

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e2837e702adace9c449771efbf2c90838eef0a05` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Isolated review, read at 2026-11-26T14:59Z. Inputs: card #37499 (body, claim 7191684203, dev report 7194444492), this PR's body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `5dbcc02b84`, `main` at `0f6a1e518f`), and the 70 check-runs on the head: 59 success, 11 skipped, none failed. Nothing was checked out, built or run; every claim below about code outside the diff is a reading of the tree at this head, and says so where it was not measured.

### ① Derived judgments

Every answer the diff moves is for a caller naming no package, a type the registry reads by package, and a name whose every holder is disabled.

1. `PUT /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME` (publish mode) over a stored package-less row: `200` to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, enable remedy. Right: the card's ruling, and the removed early return in `packagelessHolderRefusal` is the premise the claim named.
2. The same save where the package-less row sits beside a disabled package's own row (the served address answers the package-less row): `200` to `409`. Right: the new call under `served.packageId === null`; it can only refuse when every holder is disabled, so the cell with an enabled holder is unmoved.
3. `PUT …?mode=draft` over a stored package-less row or draft: `200` to `409`. Right: the call site was already there and already passed `active.unbound || drafts.unbound`; only the judgment moved.
4. `DELETE /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME` over a stored package-less row: `200` to `409`, nothing deleted. Right, and the cell the card grades p1.
5. `DELETE …?state=draft`: over a package-less draft `200` to `409`; with a package-less active row and no draft, the `?package=` refusal or the no-op receipt to the enable refusal. Right: the `customized` field carries the active row into the disabled-holders judgment without switching off the two-enabled-holders check that `unbound` gates.
6. The same through in-process `saveMetaItem` / `deleteMetaItem` with `packageId` absent or `null`. Right: both transports end in these two facets; neither forwards a caller-stated `source`.
7. Refusal shape: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, an `Error` carrying `code` and `status`, no new code, no package named: the same family and shape as `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal`. Right. The fixed text is 386 characters, so the type and the name share 114 before the 500-character cut, and the fix leads.
8. Not moved, each read in the code (the sealed types from the dev's measurement; their refusal answers above this block): a name no package holds (`every.length === 0`); a package-less row at a name an enabled package holds, the two-enabled-holders cell included (the `!address.unbound` guard keeps the `resolveItem` skip); a name only disabled packages hold with no package-less row or draft (ruling A's sentence); every write naming a package (each call site is inside `request.packageId == null`); a type the registry does not read by package; the sealed types; the server-stated rewrites (`source` set, `package-duplicate`). Right.
9. `@objectstack/spec`: one semantic entry joins step 19's list (upgrade guide and `spec-changes` projections). No key, def or export moves; `disabledHoldersCustomizationRefusal` and the widened `address` parameter are not re-exported from the package entry, so no API surface moves.
10. NOT derived, though the ADR note reads as if it were: the per-item publish and the per-item rollback naming no package. See S1.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` stand on the claim, the PR body and the changeset, and they are right: no published schema or accept-set moves, and a write an author could send is now refused. `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, as the changeset has them. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, every moved answer before and after, the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker naming the registered id; `Check Changeset` and every lint leg are green on the head, and the dev's derived gates list `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` at exit 0. objectql and runtime change tests only and owe no changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- L2 owed and not arranged by the dev: this record.
- Tier H: confirmed. The note sits under a Decision heading (D3) and the diff carries code and a narrowing, so the low-risk arm does not apply whatever this record's `Security-touching:` line reads. That line reads `no` because no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour: the refusal is a `409` on write doors and moves no grant or capability gate.
- File surface beyond the claim (the spec entry, the objectql pin): accepted. The narrowed declaration owes the entry, and the objectql test pinned the old `200`.
- Card-body writes on #34260 and #36229: the seat's. With S1 open, "no write lands on a hidden item" is not yet true of the tree; word those criteria accordingly.
- Delete and discard pinned through the REST route and in-process `deleteMetaItem`: accepted. The dispatcher answers `405` to a `DELETE` on a metadata item (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`), so there is no third door to pin.
- Branch name, PR attribution footer, `test:repo` left to CI (`Test Core` 10/10 green): accepted.
- Self-decided: the refusal names no package. Accepted: the neighbouring refusal and the epic's rule (a disabled package is never named). Cost noted as N5.
- Self-decided: the `?package=` refusal is kept where no package-less row is stored. Accepted: that is ruling A (#34144), and the card rules out `?package=` only "here", where a hidden row would gain a second row beside it. Edge noted as N6.
- Self-decided: the draft discard widens to the active rows only when a package-less row or draft is involved. Accepted: it keeps every other discard cell where it was, and the merged candidate set can only add holders to the judgment.
- Dev observation (a `doc` bare read served a package-less row after a restart where it served the package's body before one, on a directly seeded row): not this PR's. A read whose answer changes across a restart is worth a card even with no door that writes the row; the seat decides the filing.
- `open_questions`, fold the `_env` draft read (#34261) here: A, leave it on its own card. It lives in other files and the claim does not cover them. The card's ruling already says which way it settles (404), so #34261 should carry that sentence.
- `dogfood_battery`: reported green on this head by the dev (487 files, 4129 tests, lock verdict exit 0). The CI dogfood shards are skipped on this head and only the aggregate reads success, so the dev's run is the dogfood evidence there is.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. It adds one keyed read of the item's active rows (`type`, `name`, `state`) to a draft discard naming no package, a row set bounded by the packages holding one name, and unions two short package-id lists in memory. `packagelessDraftAddress` reads the same rows a moment earlier; reusing them is a tidy-up, not a push-down question.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. One should-fix, owing a delta review.

**S1 (should-fix) — the ADR note says every write naming no package is refused; two write doors naming no package are not asked the judgment at this head.** The note reads "it hides with its holder, on the reads and on the writes alike", "Every write naming no package is refused … : the publish-mode save, the draft save, the delete and the draft discard", and "Re-enable serves the row untouched". Read in the tree, not run:

- The per-item publish. `POST /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME/publish` with no `?package=` reaches `publishMetaItem` and `promoteDraftForPublish` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts`). It resolves its draft through `packagelessDraftAddress` and never asks `packagelessHolderRefusal`; the file holds no disabled-holder judgment, and neither does the REST route. In the cell this PR's own third pin stores (a package-less draft of a name only the disabled D ships, alone or beside the package-less row) the address is the package-less draft, so the promotion writes the package-less active row: the hidden row is edited unseen, and the row the next enable serves is not the one stored before the disable.
- The per-item rollback. `rollbackMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts`) with no package named takes the binding of the stored row at the read address, which is the package-less row when that is the row stored, and restores onto it. No disabled-holder judgment is asked there or in `protocol-history-slots.ts`.

Neither door is among the card's four, so the card's Done-when is met by this diff, and this is not graded as a failure of the fix. The finding is on the note: it records a universal the tree does not hold, and it is the text a maintainer approves as the contract. Fix, either way: (a) measure both doors in cell 1 first, then word the note as the four doors it closes, name the per-item publish and the rollback as not judged yet, and cite their card; or (b) close both here through the same judgment and pin them. One clause should also say that the server-stated rewrites (`source` set, `package-duplicate`) are not asked, by design.

Per file, against the code and the scenario it is accepted against:

- `19.disabled-holder-package-less-row-bare-write-refused.ts`: holds. The major is right at 19. The file name takes the protocol major (`entries/README.md`); `PROTOCOL_VERSION` reads `19.0.0` on `main` since #37314; `registry.ts.template` carries step 19 and says later v19-line entries are added as files; Changesets is in pre mode with a pending spec major (`.changeset/37223-v19-line-opens.md`), so a `minor` landing now publishes in the 19 prerelease line; `19.data-table-staged-edit-retired.ts` (#37437) is the precedent. `build-schemas.ts` on `main` still derives `CURRENT_MAJOR` from `package.json` (18.6.0, so 18), but it prescribes a major only for retired-key and retired-def files, and this PR retires neither. The id matches the file name and the changeset marker. Surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria name the four doors and the three unmoved cells as the code has them, and claim nothing about the two doors of S1. No tombstone and no conversion is owed: no key or stored shape moves.
- ADR-0150, the D3 note, sentence by sentence. The D4 quotation is verbatim. The maintainer's words are the card's. The writes bullet, the draft bullet and the re-enable bullet agree with the four call sites and with `everyRowBytes` in the pins, subject to S1. The "what this replaces" paragraph is the card's measurement and the removed line. Controls 1 to 3 agree with the code and have pins. The `_env` control agrees with the tree: the qualified route is a `GET` only. `Code:` and `Pins:` name symbols and test titles that exist at this head.
- `protocol-save.ts`: agrees with the contract. Removing the early return alone would have moved the two-enabled-holders cell; the `!address.unbound` guard on the `resolveItem` arm keeps it. The environment's own item still returns first. The new refusal is chosen only after the every-holder-disabled test passes. The publish-mode call under a null served address cannot fire while an enabled package holds the name. Tried and not broken: a save naming a package, `packageId: null` spelled out, a row bound to a disabled holder's customization pair beside the package-less row, a registry without the holder reads.
- `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`: agrees. The active delete passes its own rows; the discard passes the merged address only when a package-less row or draft exists, so no cell without one moves. Tried and not broken: the discard with an enabled holder and a package-less active row (the two-enabled check still runs, as before), the discard of a name no package holds.
- The two test files: the pins assert status, code, the leading words, the absence of every package id, the stored bytes of every row, and the re-enable round trip, on both transports and both registration orders; the control is split as the card asks. See N7 for what they do not hold.

Nits (none moves the head by itself; fix on the next push of the note, or leave as accepted deviations or follow-up cards):

- N1 (nit, ADR prose): the reads bullet is silent on the draft reads. At this head the draft read at `_env` still answers `409` (the PR body's "Not folded", #34261) and the bare draft read answers `404 NO_DRAFT`. Name both, with the card.
- N2 (nit, ADR prose): "Unchanged, and pinned as controls" heads five bullets, and the sealed-type and `_env` bullets are measurements with no pin in this diff. Say measured there.
- N3 (nit, ADR prose): the first sentence states D4's customization rule without D4's 2026-11-24 exception (the platform's own record). A parenthesis would keep the two notes from reading as a contradiction.
- N4 (nit, entry prose): `surface` reads "every installed package holding it has disabled"; "is disabled" is meant.
- N5 (nit, refusal text): "Enable the package that holds …" is singular and definite where several disabled packages may hold the name, and the packages list it points at shows which are disabled, not which holds the name. The changeset and the entry say "a package". Accepted with the no-package-named rule.
- N6 (nit, door symmetry): two cells still answer another refusal's sentence. With only a package-less draft stored, the publish-mode save and the active delete answer ruling A's `?package=` sentence while a hidden draft sits beside the row it would write. With two disabled packages' own rows and a package-less row, the delete answers the two-binding refusal, naming both packages, before the holder judgment is reached, where the save answers the enable sentence. Both refuse and write nothing.
- N7 (nit, tests): the new runtime pins lay their rows straight into the store, so they hold the state in which the registry has not read the row. The door-written state is pinned only by the objectql test, for the save and the delete of a code-shipped holder; the restart reading is the dev's measurement and has no pin. For the authored-holder arm the registry-read state is not shown either way: a package overlay slot adds no composite holder, so `getEnvironmentScopedItem` may answer the package-less row there and the judgment would return before the holders are counted. A reboot arm on these four pins would settle it.

Out of the diff, read and not reviewed:

- The code half of S1: `protocol-history-and-publish.ts` and `protocol-package-commits.ts`.
- `build-schemas.ts` reads its major from the package label (18) while entries now take the protocol major (19): the next retirement card will be handed an `18.` file name by one gate and a step-19 home by the template. Worth a look for an existing card.
- `listDrafts` filters a draft by its own package id only, so a package-less draft of a name only disabled packages hold still appears in the drafts list. Read, not run; it belongs to topic #36229.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `450813bf0bd2789c250675c48d53db8c20084f66`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.disabled-holder-package-less-row-bare-write-refused.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts

Isolated delta review, read at 2026-11-26T15:53Z. It follows record 7195624788 on head `7e66896196`. Inputs: card #37499 (body, claim 7191684203, dev report 7194444492), this PR's body and file list, the earlier record, the diff between the two heads in full, the net diff against `main`, and the 70 check-runs on this head: 59 success, 11 skipped, none failed. The two cards the reworded note cites (#37608, #34261) were read as its citations. Nothing was checked out, built or run. Every claim about code is a reading of the tree at this head.

The delta is 8 added and 6 removed lines over two files: the D3 note in ADR-0150, and one string in the migration entry. No other file differs between the two heads, so the four implementing files are byte-identical to the ones the earlier record read.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The delta moves no accept-set and no public surface. Judgments 1 to 9 of the earlier record stand unchanged.
2. The entry's `surface` string changes its wording, so the upgrade guide and `spec-changes` projections carry the new sentence. The id, the file name and the changeset marker do not move. Right.
3. The earlier record's item 10 (the per-item publish and the per-item rollback are not derived) is now what the note itself says. Right.
4. NOT derived, though the note and the entry read as if it were: the `409` with the enable remedy for an item the ADR-0146 D11 close already answers. See S2.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` stand on the claim, the PR body and the changeset. The changeset was not touched by the delta: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, one ADR-0087 marker naming the registered id. The entry's reworded string publishes inside the spec minor already declared. `Check Changeset` and every lint leg are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The fix chosen for S1 is rewording, with the two doors moved to card #37608: accepted. #37608 is open, p1, blocked on this PR's merge, names both doors and makes measuring them its first step. The fix did not measure them before wording the note, which the earlier record's option asked for. The note says so itself ("Read in the code, not measured") and claims only that each door can still write the row. Accepted on that wording.
- "The delta is prose only": nearly. One hunk edits a string literal in a source file of a published package (`packages/spec`). It moves no logic. `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` 10/10 and the lint legs are green on this head.
- The PR body's verification readings name the earlier head. For this review it does not matter: the suites, the ablation and the typechecks measured files the delta does not touch, and this head's own check-runs answer the gates the two changed files can move. For landing it does matter. The land gate (`scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`, read and not run) takes the `dogfood_battery` sha from the newest dev report on the card and accepts it only when it is the head, or is reached from the head over merges of the base alone. The newest report (7194444492) names `7e66896196`, and this head is an ordinary commit on top of it. CI skips the dogfood shards on this head, as on the last. So a battery run on the final head, and a report carrying it, are owed before the land. S2's fix moves the head again, so run it once, after that fix. The body's heading "Dogfood battery on the head" should name the head it ran on.
- The PR body's maintainer summary (its second line) still reads as the whole write half of the rule. With #37608 open, it should say four doors and name the card. A body edit, which moves no head.
- Card-body writes on #34260 and #36229: the seat's, as before. The note now gives the wording: the criterion holds for the four writes and not for the two #37608 carries.
- Earlier nits: N1 to N4 are taken in this delta and read right. N5 to N7 were not touched and stand as accepted deviations or follow-up cards.
- `open_questions` (fold #34261 here): answered A in the earlier record; unchanged.
- `main` has moved (`54d6726c09`) and #37576 touched ADR-0150 there. The PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no code.
- Tier H and the `Security-touching:` line: as the earlier record has them. No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour; the note names the stored flow-credential move only as a server rewrite that is not asked this judgment.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed

No must-fix. One should-fix, owing a delta review.

Why S1 is closed. The note no longer states a universal. It says the row hides "on the reads, and on the four writes this note closes", heads the bullet "Four writes naming no package are refused", bounds the re-enable bullet to those four, names the per-item publish and the per-item rollback as not judged yet with their symbols, files and card, and adds the clause on the server-stated rewrites. Each new sentence was read against the tree:

- `promoteDraftForPublish` is in `protocol-history-and-publish.ts` and `rollbackMetaItem` is in `protocol-package-commits.ts`. `packagelessHolderRefusal` is called from `protocol-save.ts` and `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` only, so neither door asks it.
- The publish takes its address from `packagelessDraftAddress` when no package is named. The rollback takes the served row's binding, else the stored row's. Each can therefore address the package-less row, as the note says.
- The rewrites clause agrees with the code. `source: 'migrate-stored'` is stated by `migrateStoredMetadata` and by the flow-credential migration, and the save's address block is skipped when `source` is set. The package duplicate passes its target package.
- #37608 carries both doors. #34261 carries the `_env` draft read.
- D4's note dated 2026-11-24 exists and excepts the platform's own record.
- The "Unchanged" list has five bullets: three with pins and two measurements, as its new heading says.

**S2 (should-fix) — the note and the entry state the `409` and its enable remedy for every name only disabled packages hold; where the ADR-0146 D11 close applies, three of the four doors answer that close first, and neither file says so.** Read in the tree, not run:

- The save door asks `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal` for both modes, ahead of all three call sites of the disabled-holders judgment (`protocol-save.ts`). The delete door asks it for the active delete, ahead of its call site (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`). The draft discard is not asked.
- That close answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. Its sentence names the base's paired package (BASE.custom) and prescribes `?package=` with that id. It applies to an item of one of the five overlay types, `dashboard` among them, that one read-only code package ships, with an ensurable pair and a recorded version, whose package-less row `os migrate packageless-overlays` would move.
